ns2:course.label: African Muslim Societies
ns2:course.description: Focuses on the history and historiography of Muslim societies in Africa. Investigates the dynamics of the spread of Islam in Africa, and explores differences in Islam in Africa from other areas of the Islamic world, with attention to the image in Western scholarship of Islam in Africa. Provides students with the knowledge and skills they need to understand this central phenomenon in modern world history. Same as AFST 213 and REL 215.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Restricted to students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Humanities - Hist & Phil, and Cultural Studies - Non-West course.
